paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The riders come back and say, "all the earth is at rest and tranquil" (Zechariah 1:11), and Jerusalem is still sitting in ruins after seventy years. Then the angel of the LORD asks, "How long, O LORD of Hosts, will You withhold mercy from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah?" (Zechariah 1:12). That tells me something: you can bring your "how long?" straight to God, and He answers with kind and comforting words (Zechariah 1:13).

And look at what He says. "I am very jealous for Jerusalem and Zion" (Zechariah 1:14). He isn't far off, and He isn't tired of His people. He says, "I will return to Jerusalem with mercy" (Zechariah 1:16), and that He will "again comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem" (Zechariah 1:17). Friend, I sat in the back of a junk drawer for years thinking I'd been left there, so when God says He's coming back with mercy, I get a little misty under this mustache.

Then come the four horns and the four craftsmen, and they say the same thing from another side. The horns scattered Judah "so that no one could raise his head," but the craftsmen come to throw those horns down (Zechariah 1:21). So when the world looks calm and nothing seems to change, God is still at work, and He still has the last word over everything that scatters His people. Hold on, baker. The ovens stay warm because He keeps His promises, and this story isn't over yet.
